picks.title: At SIGGRAPH, NVIDIA advances graphics and simulation with agentic and physical AI
picks.excerpt: At SIGGRAPH 2026 NVIDIA unveiled neural-rendering breakthroughs and world foundation models (Cosmos 3 Edge) for real-time 4K content creation with more artistic control, plus 22 graphics-research advances. It also expanded Model Context Protocol integrations so AI agents can work directly inside creative tools like Blender, Unreal Engine and Adobe Creative Cloud while keeping creative decisions under human supervision.
picks.rationale: Neural rendering plus MCP agents working directly inside Unreal/Blender is a concrete engine-pipeline shift for game artists; no prior SIGGRAPH/NVIDIA card in the games-section history.

picks.title: New method teaches AI to make 2D designs 3D
picks.excerpt: Researchers demonstrate a new AI method that converts flat 2D designs and drawings into fully realized 3D models — a capability with direct implications for game asset-creation pipelines, letting concept art be lifted into game-ready geometry with far less manual modeling.
picks.rationale: A new concept-art-to-3D-geometry method directly changes how asset artists move from sketch to game-ready model; novel research from a credible outlet. Distinct accent from the other games picks.

picks.title: Ethical, low-power, and on-device: Studio Atelico's vision for the future of generative AI
picks.excerpt: Studio Atelico lays out a vision for ethical, low-power, on-device generative AI in games. Its debut title, Bobium Brawlers, blends "classic game design with the possibilities of AI" — and, importantly, all the artists on the project are paid, positioning the studio against the extractive-AI backlash in the industry.
picks.rationale: An on-device, artist-paid genAI model offers a practical alternative stance for studios weighing how to adopt AI responsibly; distinct outlet and angle. Distinct accent from the other games picks.

picks.title: Persona and Shin Megami Tensei artist isn't using generative AI in his next game following backlash to his last 2 deckbuilders
picks.excerpt: Veteran Persona and Shin Megami Tensei artist Kazuma Kaneko says he will not use generative AI in his next game after fan backlash to his last two AI-assisted deckbuilders, noting "it's quicker for me to draw it myself" — a pointed data point on where hand-craft still beats AI in game art workflows.
picks.rationale: A marquee artist reversing course on genAI is a concrete signal on where hand-craft still outpaces AI in game art; timely, distinct outlet. Distinct accent from the other games picks.
